note: (a) Reference 25,503 kt. One at a time: not additive, not a joint interval. "No effect": every case within 0.01% of the Reference. Not shown: the superseded-setting rows (completion rate 0.95, completion lag 0 months and the never-absorbed overbuild) and the overbuild gap measured against the 2026 requirement (+0.0028%); no census under-construction correction (+0.0000%); maintenance event timing L / n (-0.6961%) (in the data file). Row notes: Living arrangements: propensities change (Stats NZ B): Stats NZ Medium B household projection (living-arrangement propensities change, modelled on the 2001–2023 censuses) instead of Medium A (propensities held at 2023): what if B happens anyway (the same path is L1 Ambitious, what if policy delivers it). Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base stochastic projection, 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median, with the household size of the Stats NZ Low / High A household projection (the same percentiles). Household size (2018–23 pace): household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-interval pace instead of the Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023. After 2048: held flat (zero slope): a zero slope imposed at 2048 and household size held constant after it instead of the 2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050. After 2048: PCHIP end slope: the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end derivative at 2048, continued linearly, instead of the 2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050. Dwelling-size reference window 2016–2025: new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology instead of the 2023–2025 mean. No starting surplus (2024–25 excess not carried): no starting surplus instead of 18,966 vacant dwellings at the start of 2026, absorbed by 2035: (the 2024–2025 building beyond the stock identity, 9,020 dwellings a year, minus the 1992–2023 census-interval mean, −463) × 2 years; carried because it exceeds the mean + 2 SD (SD 3,038). 2026 overbuild booked as stock-neutral redevelopment: the 2026 overbuild (building above need in 2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ = 0.43) replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to the stock: no surplus, so no absorption payback and no soil carbon loss on it. Completion rate (0.93–0.96): 0.93 / 0.96 of consented dwellings completed instead of 0.945. Starting surplus minus 2 SD: a starting surplus of 6,812 dwellings (only the excess above the mean + 2 SD) instead of 18,966. Vacancy rate: 1986–2023 census mean: the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the 2023 census value (5.39%). Surplus absorbed (by 2030–by 2045): the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035. Completion lag (15–19 months): consents lagged 15 / 19 months instead of 17. No 2026 data (consents to Dec 2025): consents to December 2025 and the projected 2026 population instead of consents to September 2026 and the observed 2026 population growth. Replacement (Low–Very High): Low: the 1991–2023 long-run net rate throughout; High (tick): the 2018–2023 rate persists; Very High: the 1991–2023 census-interval trend continues; instead of the 2018–2023 rate fading to the long-run rate with a 10-year half-life. Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): 5 / 15 years instead of 10. Soil order (Raw–Organic): the soil carbon loss of the lowest (Raw) / highest (Organic) soil order on every new footprint instead of the area-weighted mean over the soil orders of the Auckland land zoned for urbanisation. Single case study (lowest–highest): the materials factor of the lowest / highest single case study of each typology instead of the pooled typology factor. Module D credit, booked at construction (not netted): the Module D credit (benefits beyond the system boundary, EN 15978) of the 2026–2050 cohorts at 2025 factors (the largest credit), booked in the construction year and subtracted; carbon only; not converted to LoE, because a consistent LoE would need Module D in the historical sector base as well. Frozen technology (2025 factors held): every factor held at 2025 instead of A1–A3 on the item paths of Horup et al. (2025) and A4–A5 falling 1% per year. Production decarbonisation: no-policy backgrounds (Horup MAX): A1-A3 of construction and in-window events x [MAX(y)/MAX(2025)] / [AVG(y)/AVG(2025)] of the 9 backgrounds (Horup et al. 2025, Table S3) from 2027: the no-climate-policy end of L10; carbon only. Carbon factors (jackknife): the lowest / highest pooled materials factor when each case study is left out in turn, instead of the pooled factor (a spread, not a confidence interval). NZ-made electricity-intensive items held at 2025 factors: items made in New Zealand with electricity-intensive production held at 2025 instead of following their Horup et al. (2025) path. A4–A5 decarbonisation (own path–held at 2025): A4–A5 on each item's own Horup et al. (2025) path / held at 2025 instead of the generic 1% per year decline (Resch et al. 2021). Soil carbon loss on all floor area, incl. replacement: soil carbon loss also on replacement floor area instead of none on rebuilt footprints. Proxy-mapped items held at 2025 factors: items mapped to a proxy material held at 2025 instead of following the proxy's path. (b) Theoretical Limit 4,177.0 kt; L10: near-zero factor on all material classes 3,907.3 kt, LoE AR 0.883, P(LoE AR <= 1) = 74.66%; L10: near-zero share 100% by 2050 4,159.5 kt, LoE AR 0.940, P(LoE AR <= 1) = 61.78%.
